answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy prices trust like saffron: scarce and slow to accumulate. Every identity starts at zero weight, and only graded work earns it, in small slices over many epochs, so a fresh alias is worthless on arrival. Earnings vest on a delay, so an attacker who spins up a thousand clones must fund a thousand histories before any can vote. One bad submission burns the stake, and the loss ripples outward like cracks in marble: aliases linked by funding or timing share the penalty. Cloning costs time and money; honesty pays from day one.
